title: Skateboarding: the greats overview
d: The greatest Skateboarding players, ranked by titles, records, and influence.
definition: The greatest Skateboarding players, ranked by titles, records, and influence.
description: The pantheon of Skateboarding is argued in every bar and barbershop, but the names in this database appear on every serious list: champions who won the biggest prizes, record-setters whose numbers still stand, and pioneers who changed how Skateboarding is played. Greatness here is measured three ways — winning, statistics, and influence — and the truest greats score on all three. Study them not to worship but to learn: every great was once a beginner who mastered fundamentals.

title: Tony Hawk
d: Tony Hawk (1978-2003): The 900 in 1999; skating's global ambassador.
definition: Tony Hawk (1978-2003): The 900 in 1999; skating's global ambassador.
description: Tony Hawk competed at the top of Skateboarding from 1978-2003, and the achievement that defines the career is this: The 900 in 1999; skating's global ambassador. What separated Tony Hawk was not one skill but the complete package — technique hardened by repetition, tactics sharpened by study, and the temperament to deliver when everything is on the line. Young players should study not just the highlights but the habits: the training volume, the professionalism, and the longevity that turned talent into legacy.

title: Tony Hawk: legacy
d: Why Tony Hawk matters to Skateboarding history.
definition: Why Tony Hawk matters to Skateboarding history.
description: The legacy of Tony Hawk in Skateboarding goes beyond the trophy count: The 900 in 1999; skating's global ambassador. Legacy is what remains when the career ends — the records that stood for decades, the style that juniors copied, the barriers broken for those who followed. Tony Hawk changed what people believed was possible in Skateboarding, and every generation since has played in the space that career opened up.
